$comment: Which hooks.json entries each client runs (BI-742D707B). hooks.json stays the one roster; this file holds only per-client delivery, matcher aliases, bundled substitutes and exclusions. Exclusion keys are Event:script (or Event:* for a whole event), and every one carries its reason. Client keys are the client kinds toolchain_convergence.DISCOVERY finds, plus grok-sandbox for Build Studio dispatch; a test fails when the two lists differ. update_agent_toolchain.py (host) and hooks/lib/grok-hook-plane.mjs (Build Studio sandbox, no Python there) both build Grok's dpf-guards.json from hooks.json minus these, and a test pins their output equal. The generated hooks/README.md renders the per-client table from this file. What a client was observed to do lives in ../client-capabilities.json; this file is what DPF chooses to wire.

codex.plane: plugin hooks/hooks.json from the Codex plugin cache (~/.codex/hooks.json only as the blocking-guard fallback)

excluded.WorktreeCreate:*: Codex does not run it: on 2026-10-14 its hook trust state listed 33 of the 34 entries and none for WorktreeCreate.

grok.plane: ~/.grok/hooks/dpf-guards.json, generated from hooks.json (Grok ignores plugin-bundled hooks, BI-883FC2FC)

grok-session-start.mjs.reason: grok-session-start.mjs runs these after probing which Grok plugins are active, so process-spine can report exposed skills honestly.
grok-session-start.mjs.purpose: Run the DPF session checks Grok needs at start

grok-sandbox.plane: /home/node/.grok/hooks/dpf-guards.json in the sandbox, generated at each dispatch from the workspace pack by hooks/lib/grok-hook-plane.mjs
